name: Victoria, BC
summary: Victoria works as a three-suite hotel stay on the Inner Harbour: BC's principal-residence rental law rules out whole houses and guest cottages, so every option here is separate kitchen suites in one hotel, which gives Scott & Andrea a true lock-off by default. The best fit is the Victoria Regent (2BR Executive Suite 307 with a 950 sq ft harbour deck plus two 1BR suites), verified at US$1,560 a night for July 4-10 (re-quoted 2026-11-15), well under the cap, with Old Town restaurants a flat 5-minute walk away. The best animal options are activities with wild animals rather than feeding: a guided sea-lion kayak paddle from Oak Bay (15 min) and a hawk walk at The Raptors (55 min), both with prices and ages unpublished; the Bug Zoo lets visitors hold insects. Bear Mountain golf is 25 min out and July highs sit around 75 F. The biggest caveat is the gathering space: no suite has a confirmed table for 8 indoors, and there are no confirmed nonstop flights from Denver or the Bay Area.

hard_constraints.notes: Airport: YYJ is about 30 min from the Inner Harbour (within 90). No nonstop from DEN or SFO/OAK/SMF was confirmed; everyone connects via Seattle (Alaska) or Vancouver (Air Canada/United), or takes the Clipper ferry from Seattle. One-stop connections were judged reasonable, so it passes. Seniors: the Inner Harbour, Wharf St and Old Town are flat; all options are hotel suites with no stairs inside, except Swans lofts (avoid for the parents). Elevators were not stated on the Victoria Regent pages read (8-storey building); Chateau Victoria's 2BR suites are on floors 16-17, so it has elevators.

rationale.lodging: 19/25: rests on Victoria Regent 2 Bedroom Executive Suite (Waterfront) + two 1BR suites, US$1,560/night (verified, C$2,228 rate re-quoted 2026-11-15), with separate kitchen suites and a 950 sq ft deck in 307, but the dining table seats 6, not 8, the executive suite is booked by phone (307 not selectable online), and elevator and adjacent placement are not stated.
rationale.town_scenery: 16/18: flat, walkable Inner Harbour and Old Town with harbour views from the lodging; it is a small city rather than a village, and parts of downtown slope.
rationale.animals: 11/18: the top two are activities with wild animals (a guided Trial Island kayak paddle among seals and sea lions, 15 min, for paddlers with some experience, and a hawk walk at The Raptors, 55 min), but neither publishes price, minimum age or 2027 dates, the paddle is watching from a kayak rather than touching, and nothing involves exotic animals beyond holding insects at the Bug Zoo.
rationale.food: 15/15: well over 10 restaurants within a 10-minute flat walk of the Victoria Regent, including Il Terrazzo and Q at the Empress for the special dinner.
rationale.other: 7/10: escape rooms, kayaking, whale watching, Butchart Gardens and a museum cover every age, but there are no nonstop flights from either origin and passports are needed.
rationale.golf: 8/9: Bear Mountain Mountain Course (25 min, C$257 peak public rate) is a memorable mountain-top course, and Olympic View (about 25 min) is a cheaper alternative with waterfalls.
rationale.weather: 5/5: July normal high about 75 F (24 C) and July is the driest month; the downtown waterfront usually runs cooler than the station figure.

animals.name: Ocean River Sports: Trial Island sea lion kayak tour
animals.what_you_do: A guided sea-kayak paddle of about 3.5 hours from Oak Bay Marina, past a bird sanctuary and through Discovery Island Marine Park to Trial Island, in drysuits. Harbour seals are regularly seen and sea lions haul out on the rocks; you watch them from the kayak.
animals.why_memorable: Paddling among hauled-out sea lions and seals is an activity with wild marine mammals, not a viewing deck.
animals.price_usd: Not published on the tour page; ask Ocean River Sports, 250-381-4233
animals.booking_difficulty: Book online; runs only on selected days because of sea state and weather, and is meant for paddlers with some previous kayaking experience. Minimum age and 2027 dates not stated. Strenuous: the parents sit this out. Beginners can take Ocean River's downtown Inner Harbour tours from 450 Swift St instead (details not read).

image.alt: Kayakers on the Trial Island sea lion tour

animals.what_you_do: Watch daily flying demonstrations, then book a hands-on session: walk through the woods with a hawk or hold a falcon or owl on a glove.
animals.why_memorable: A hawk landing on your own glove in the forest is a real encounter, not a viewing.
animals.price_usd: Not published; one undated TripAdvisor review cites $110 for the Closest Encounter
animals.booking_difficulty: Hands-on sessions need advance booking; ages, prices and July 2027 slots not published (call 250-746-0372). Daily demos stated on the operator site, re-read 2026-11-15; no closure notice. Also runs five-day kids' summer camps and a week-long falconry course (dates not published).

image.alt: Bird of prey at The Raptors, Duncan

animals.name: Alpine Stables trail rides, Cobble Hill
animals.what_you_do: Guided horseback rides through rainforest: a 1-hour Beginner Trail Ride for families, a 2-hour rainforest ride, or a 3-hour ride to a summit with ocean and valley views.
animals.why_memorable: Riding a horse to a viewpoint over the valley is an outing with the animals rather than a petting stop.
animals.price_usd: Not shown on the listing ('N/A'); the FareHarbor booking page did not load
animals.booking_difficulty: Book through FareHarbor; Beginner Trail Ride from age 5; longer rides need an age and riding-ability check with the stable. Weight limits, address and July 2027 dates not stated. Drive time to Cobble Hill is an estimate via the Malahat.

animals.name: Victoria Bug Zoo
animals.what_you_do: Walk through a small indoor insect and arachnid collection with an educator, who brings out animals for visitors to hold.
animals.why_memorable: Holding leaf insects and stick insects downtown, on a rainy hour or any day.
animals.price_usd: Prices vary by age; not listed on the home page
animals.booking_difficulty: Walk-in or book online; no closure notice. Mon-Fri 11-4, Sat-Sun 10-4; summer hours from June 30. Holding arachnids is 18+, so Ethan and Aubrey can hold insects only.

animals.name: Victoria Butterfly Gardens
animals.what_you_do: Walk through a tropical indoor garden with free-flying butterflies and birds, a flamingo, tortoises, poison dart frogs and a dwarf caiman.
animals.why_memorable: Butterflies may land on you; easy flat indoor walk for the parents, near Butchart Gardens.
animals.price_usd: Adult C$20, student (13-17) C$16, senior C$16, child (5-12) C$9.50
animals.booking_difficulty: Open 7 days; walk-in tickets. Pair with Butchart Gardens.

golf.name: Bear Mountain: Mountain Course
golf.what_you_do: 18 holes on a Nicklaus-designed course climbing Bear Mountain in Langford, with GPS carts.
golf.why_memorable: Big elevation changes and views over Victoria and the Olympic Mountains; one of BC's most awarded resort courses.
golf.price_usd: C$257 public peak rate (May 1-Oct 31), twilight C$177 from 2 pm, junior C$62 from noon; power cart C$28 extra and mandatory (rates page: 'power carts are mandatory'), so about C$285 with cart
golf.booking_difficulty: Book by phone 250-744-2327 or online; the rates page shows no year. Junior rate asks for a driver's licence, which Ethan (15) will not have.

golf.name: Olympic View Golf Club
golf.what_you_do: 18 public holes in the Westshore hills, with twelve lakes and two waterfalls.
golf.why_memorable: A 60-foot waterfall behind the 17th green and Olympic Mountain views, at a fraction of Bear Mountain's fee.
golf.price_usd: Dynamic pricing; club's 2026 rates page (High Season Apr 1-Nov 1) shows green fees from C$125, twilight C$80, sunset C$60; 2027 rates not published
golf.booking_difficulty: Online tee times; the club charges a C$20 advance booking fee for bookings more than 15 days ahead (2026 page; GolfBC URL now redirects to olympicviewgolf.com).

activities.name: Butchart Gardens
activities.details: 55-acre historic gardens in Brentwood Bay; paved paths and wheelchairs make it the easiest big outing for Sam and Karen. July hours and 2027 rates were not on the home page; check the Hours & Rates page. Pair with the Butterfly Gardens nearby.
activities.found_via: TripAdvisor top things to do (via search snippets)

activities.name: Quest Reality Games escape rooms
activities.details: 60-minute indoor escape rooms near Bastion Square, about 5 min from the Victoria Regent; family-friendly themes, teens 14+ can play without adults. Prices not checked. Arcadia (escape rooms, VR, arcade) is another downtown option.

activities.name: Prince of Whales whale watching
activities.details: 3-4 hour boat or Zodiac trips from 812 Wharf St, below the Empress, to look for orcas, humpbacks, seals and sea lions; July is peak whale season. C$179 Zodiac / C$189 half-day covered boat per adult plus tax (seasonal pricing); private Zodiac C$2,000 per boat. Hourly departures; book a few days ahead in July. Viewing only, so it sits outside the animal ranking. The dock is reached by stairs to the lower causeway; the covered boat suits the parents better than the Zodiac.

activities.name: Royal BC Museum and IMAX
activities.details: Natural and human history museum beside the Parliament Buildings, about 12 min flat walk; TripAdvisor users have voted it a top museum in Canada. Elevators inside; check which galleries are open during its modernization.

activities.name: Fisherman's Wharf and Inner Harbour stroll
activities.details: Flat harbour-front walk past the Empress and Parliament to the floating homes and food kiosks at Fisherman's Wharf; Government St shopping and the Old Town boutiques for Karen, Jenna and Andrea. Feeding the wharf seals is banned (earlier research).

shopping_exploring: Government St, Lower Johnson St (LoJo) boutiques, Market Square and Chinatown's Fan Tan Alley are all within a 10-minute flat walk of the Victoria Regent. Craigdarroch Castle is a popular tour but has many interior stairs.

restaurants.name: Red Fish Blue Fish
restaurants.notes: Seafood takeout from a container kitchen on the Wharf St pier (1006 Wharf St); outdoor seating only.

restaurants.name: Swans Brewpub
restaurants.notes: Brewpub with 58 beers on tap at 1601 Store St, under the Swans Hotel.

restaurants.name: Finn's Seafood Chops Cocktails
restaurants.notes: Seafood and steak at 1208 Wharf St, next door to the Victoria Regent, harbour views.

restaurants.name: Nautical Nellies
restaurants.notes: Waterfront seafood and steakhouse at 1001 Wharf St with a broad menu.

restaurants.name: Il Terrazzo
restaurants.notes: Northern Italian in a courtyard off Waddington Alley, 555 Johnson St; dinner nightly from 4 pm, reservations highly recommended (250-361-0028); prices not published. Alternative: Q at the Empress (OpenTable: C$51 and over).

restaurants.name: Jam Cafe
restaurants.notes: Brunch spot open 8 am-2 pm weekdays, 8-3 weekends; expect lines. Street address not on its home page.

july.notes: Environment Canada 1981-2010 normals for 'Victoria' via Current Results: 24 C / 12 C. NOAA 1991-2020 via Extreme Weather Watch gives 23.7 C / 11.7 C. These are airport/inland figures; the downtown waterfront is usually cooler. July is the driest month; a rain-day count was not found.

flights.den: No nonstop found. One stop via Seattle (Alaska) or Vancouver (United or Air Canada to YVR, then Air Canada to YYJ); or fly to SEA and take the Victoria Clipper ferry to the Inner Harbour.
flights.bay_area: No nonstop confirmed from SFO, OAK or SMF. Alaska sells SFO-YYJ (fares from about $187-198 one way) with a Seattle connection; Air Canada via YVR.

logistics.car_needed: Not downtown; everything in Old Town and the Inner Harbour is walkable. One rental car for Butchart Gardens, Bear Mountain, Olympic View, Oak Bay Marina, Alpine Stables and The Raptors in Duncan.
logistics.notes: Passports needed for all eight. The Clipper and Harbour Air floatplanes land in the Inner Harbour, a few minutes from the hotels. The Malahat highway to Duncan is about 55 min each way.

caveats: BC's principal-residence rule means no whole houses or guest cottages; all options are hotel suites (the James Bay Inn backup's cottage is part of the inn).
No suite has a confirmed indoor table for 8 except Penthouse 800 at the Victoria Regent.
No confirmed nonstop flights from Denver or the Bay Area; everyone connects and needs a passport.
The top animal options (sea-lion kayak, hawk walk, horseback) publish no prices, ages or 2027 dates; the kayak tour expects some paddling experience.
The Oswego Hotel's own domain is parked; its status could not be confirmed, so it was left out.

brochure.tagline: Harbour walks, whale boats, gardens and a hawk walk
brochure.intro: Victoria is a flat, walkable harbour city where a week runs on short strolls, boat rides and good dinners. Base yourselves on the Inner Harbour, then take a car out to Butchart Gardens, the golf courses and a hawk walk.
highlights: Kayak among sea lions and seals from Oak Bay
Whale-watching boats leave from the Inner Harbour
Walk with a hawk at The Raptors
Mountain-top golf at Bear Mountain, 25 minutes away
Old Town restaurants a short flat walk from the hotels
pros: Flat harbour-front walks, easy for everyone
Whales, gardens, golf and a museum all close by
Kitchens in every suite, so breakfasts at home are easy
Plenty of restaurants within a short walk
July is the driest month, with highs around 75 F
cons: No nonstop flights; one connection each way
Hotel suites only, with no air conditioning at the Victoria Regent
A rental car helps for Butchart, golf and The Raptors

stays.name: Victoria Regent Waterfront Hotel & Suites: Executive Suite 307 + two 1BR suites
stays.title: Victoria Regent Waterfront Hotel & Suites
stays.blurb: Kitchen suites on the Inner Harbour, with Finn's restaurant next door and Old Town a short walk away. The big suite has a wrap-around deck over the water.
highlights: 950 sq ft deck on the 2-bedroom suite

stays.title: The Parkside Hotel & Spa
stays.blurb: An all-suite hotel with an on-site spa, a pool and hot tub, and rooftop fire pits. Downtown and the harbour are a short walk.

stays.name: Chateau Victoria Hotel & Suites: 2BR suite + two 1BR suites
stays.title: Chateau Victoria Hotel & Suites
stays.blurb: A downtown high-rise a few minutes from the Inner Harbour, with the two-bedroom suites on the 16th and 17th floors.

things_to_do.name: Sea lion kayak tour to Trial Island
things_to_do.blurb: A guided paddle of about 3.5 hours from Oak Bay, 15 minutes away, to watch seals and sea lions on the rocks. Runs on selected days; some kayaking experience needed.

image.alt: Kayakers on the Trial Island sea lion tour

things_to_do.name: A hawk walk at The Raptors
things_to_do.blurb: Daily flying shows near Duncan, about 55 minutes away, plus booked sessions to walk with a hawk or hold a falcon or owl.

image.alt: Bird of prey at The Raptors, Duncan

things_to_do.name: Victoria Bug Zoo
things_to_do.blurb: A small downtown insect collection where an educator lets visitors hold leaf and stick insects.

things_to_do.name: Whale watching from the Inner Harbour
things_to_do.blurb: A 3-4 hour boat or Zodiac trip with Prince of Whales to look for orcas, humpbacks and seals. The covered boat is easier for the grandparents.

things_to_do.name: Golf at Bear Mountain
things_to_do.blurb: A Nicklaus-designed mountain course 25 minutes away with views over Victoria and the Olympic Mountains.

things_to_do.name: Butchart Gardens
things_to_do.blurb: 55 acres of historic gardens on paved paths, with wheelchairs available.

things_to_do.name: Harbour tour on the Victoria Harbour Ferry
things_to_do.blurb: A 45-minute boat tour from the Empress dock, running daily from February through October.

image.alt: Victoria Harbour Ferry on the harbour

things_to_do.name: Fisherman's Wharf
things_to_do.blurb: A flat harbour-front walk to the floating homes and food kiosks, with seafood to eat outdoors.

things_to_do.name: Royal BC Museum
things_to_do.blurb: Walk-through galleries beside the Parliament Buildings, with an IMAX theatre nearby.

image.alt: Mammoth display at the Royal BC Museum

things_to_do.name: Escape rooms near Bastion Square
things_to_do.blurb: 60-minute indoor puzzle rooms with family-friendly themes, about 5 minutes from the harbour.
